newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Police link Mafia to Brazil corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: Police link Mafia to Brazil corruption scandal.

text.p: Brazilian police investigating the country's biggest-ever corruption scandal said on Thursday they had evidence linking a murdered aide of disgraced former President Fernando Collor with the Italian Mafia.

Detectives went to Rome last week to see details of $7.8 million in bank transfers between an account of Collor's former campaign manager Paulo Cesar Farias and known Italian drug traffickers, federal police director Vicente Chelotti said.
The transactions were uncovered by Italian police tracing the origin of deposits in Mafia accounts. "We cannot say these were the only transfers," Chelotti told reporters.
The account in question was located in Holland, but Italian police had found evidence of six accounts in Farias' name in Switzerland and several others in the United States, he said.

The finds came four years after police began investigating an alleged influence-peddling scheme believed to have been masterminded by Farias and which forced Collor to resign in 1992. The transfers represented the first proof of an overseas connection to the scam, a Justice Ministry spokesman said.
Despite long-standing suspicions that Farias associated with international drug traffickers, there had been no hard evidence of a link until now, the spokesman said.

Brazilian authorities would officially ask their Italian counterparts for copies of the evidence next week to help their attempts to locate and recover cash taken out of the country, Chelotti said. "We want to find out who is benefitting from this money," he said.
The story of Farias, best known by his initials P.C., has fascinated Brazilians every bit as much as the ups and downs of his former boss who now lives in self-imposed exile in Miami.
